edges.effect_quant: The occupational literature consistently links repeated hand-arm vibration exposure with a materially higher risk of the vascular and neurologic syndrome that bears its name.
edges.population: workers exposed to vibrating hand tools
edges.mechanism: Repeated vibration can damage digital vessels, peripheral nerves, and soft tissue in the hand-arm system over time. This is one of the more direct exposure-disease pathways in occupational medicine, with the mechanism and the epidemiology pointing the same way.
edges.summary: The best current synthesis found that workplace hand-arm vibration exposure is associated with higher occurrence of hand-arm vibration syndrome. Earlier pooled and review-level literature supports the same conclusion, so this is a straightforward harmful occupational relationship rather than a subtle or disputed one.
edges.caveats: Risk depends heavily on cumulative dose, tool type, cold exposure, and preventive controls. Some older studies use variable clinical definitions, which affects the exact estimated magnitude more than the direction.
